confirmed.title: 'bridge_metal_25 x2' (4 of the 12 rollout sites) cannot be expressed: model, channel and seals all centre on the same site point
confirmed.scenario: Rollout sites #4, #8, #11 and #13 (crossings-ev106.csv, plan 'bridge_metal_25 x2'). The schema allows one model per site, and the model is centred on (x, z) (lines 56-57). The channel and seal grid is built around that same point (lines 78-81, 87, 92, 105). Encoding x2 as two entries at C ± 12.5·d (the only way to get two end-to-end spans) moves each channel axis and each seal band 12.5 m along the road. The embankment over the real stream under the joint stays uncut, and pond seals land beside the road 17-22 m from the stream. Encoding it as one entry places a single 25 m span where the plan asks for 50 m; the 1:2 channel banks then run past the abutments (see the medium finding).
confirmed.verdict:
The defect is real: bridges_v31.py has no way to place the 'bridge_metal_25 x2' sites correctly. It affects 4 of the 12 rollout sites (#4, #8, #11, #13). It does not affect the pilot, which is a single bridge_wood_25 (sites-pilot.json).

What the code does: the schema takes one model per site, and that model is centred on the site point C = (s.x, s.z) (tools/terrain/bridges_v31.py:56-57). The channel uses the same point: the grid at :78-80 and t/q at :81 are measured from (s.x, s.z) with no separate water-axis point. So does the seal grid (:103-105). The frozen-vertex exception `|sroad| <= flat` (:92-93, :98) also uses that point, and for metal flat = 12.5 - 6.5 = 6 m. The deploy plan calls for this tool on the 015 bridges ("desplegar con tools/terrain/bridges_v31.py", HANDOFF.md:19), and 4 of those are metal x2 (evidence/v31-pond-layer-2026-10-13/README.md:93).
- Two entries at C ± 12.5·d: each channel and seal band moves 12.5·sin(angle) m off the real stream, about 9-12 m for crossing angles of 47-83°. The joint at C also falls outside both entries' |sroad| <= 6 m zones, so frozen road vertices over the real stream cannot be cut.
- One entry at C: the channel is right, but it is a single 25 m span where the plan asks for 50 m.

How I checked: I ran the unchanged tool in my scratch directory on ev108-kit/terrain-ev108.npz and envelope-ev108.npy, with sites #4, #8, #11 and #13 from crossings-ev106.csv in both encodings. I then measured vertices with |q_true| <= W/2 and within 7 m of the road axis at the real crossing.
- Variant A (two entries at C ± 12.5·d):
  - #4: [7.4, 7.39, 7.4, 7.38] -> [3.4, 7.39, 7.4, 7.38]
  - #8: [12.28, 12.2, 11.83] -> [12.28, 12.2, 6.78]
  - #11: [11.34, 11.34] unchanged
  - #13: 4 of 6 vertices left at about 8.1
  - New seal cells (32-42 per site) span q_true from about -21.5 to +21.7 m, which puts pond seals beside the road.
- Variant B (one entry per site): the real axis opens to the bed (#4 -> [7.4, 1.95, 1.95, 1.95], #11 -> [2.5, 2.5], #13 -> 1.27 under the road). Seals stay within about ±10 m, but it is a single span.

These numbers match the reviewer's. All runs classified the water as pond, so there is no sea-mode confound.

Not checked: whether a manual workaround outside the tool (editing records.json to add a second span) is intended. The code itself has no field to separate the span centre from the water-axis point.

confirmed.title: Report metrics wrong: metal deck_top_mid is the truss top; channel_ground_max_under_deck samples the stream far from the deck
confirmed.scenario: deck_top_mid = pos.y + deck_max, and deck_max is the max y of the whole roadway LOD (line 37). For bridge_metal_25 that is the truss top chord (12.415), not the deck (8.055), so the reported deck is 4.36 m too high. The `under` mask (line 110) is |s| <= flat and |q| <= W/2, with no bound across the road. On near-perpendicular crossings it is a strip along the stream reaching the window edge (|t| up to about 55 m), so the 'under deck' maximum reports uncut ground far up- or downstream. A clearance or gate check reading report.json would get wrong numbers.
confirmed.verdict:
The defect is real, but it only affects report.json. Terrain, envelope, records and the staged WRP do not change. I reran bridges_v31.py on the pilot inputs into scratch, and the records came out identical to bridges/records.json. Nothing in the repo reads these two fields except evidence/v31-pond-layer-2026-10-13/bridges/report.json (checked with grep).

(1) deck_top_mid, tools/terrain/bridges_v31.py:37 and :112. deck_max is the max y over the whole roadway LOD (3e15) taken from the ODOL. bridge_wood_25: the LOD has 8 vertices, y in {0.23, 2.45}. That is a ramp to a flat crest between x = ±9.3, so 2.45 really is the mid-deck top and the pilot's 4.88 is correct. bridge_metal_25: 56 vertices, y in {6.37, 6.55, 7.07, 8.05, 12.36, 12.42}. end_y = 8.055 but deck_max = 12.415, which is the truss top. So for every metal site in the rollout (4, 8, 11, 13, all 'bridge_metal_25 x2'), deck_top_mid comes out 4.36 m too high.

(2) channel_ground_max_under_deck, line 110. The `under` mask only bounds |sroad| <= flat and |q| <= W/2. On a near-perpendicular crossing both of those measure the same direction, so t is bounded only by the window. Reproduced on the pilot 015-15: the mask covers 34 vertices with max |t| = 77.8 m. The reported 2.88 is the vertex at t = -29.6, s = -1.5, which is outside CUT_T and was never cut. Restricted to |t| <= 25, all 4 vertices under the deck are at bed 0.0. So the pilot report says the ground under the deck is at 2.88, but it is really at 0.0. The rollout reports will be wrong the same way wherever crossing angles are near 90°, which is most of them (57-88°).

Low severity: the placed geometry, the cut, the seals and the staging are all correct. But a clearance or gate check run on the rollout's report.json would read wrong numbers.

confirmed.title: v31_bridge_cut is overwritten, so a rollout run on EV108 erases the pilot's cut layer
confirmed.scenario: arrays['v31_bridge_cut'] = H != H0 marks only the current run's changes. The rollout input (terrain-ev108.npz) already carries the pilot's 23 flagged vertices, and the output records none of them. The pilot cut then disappears from the independent-layer record that a later regeneration would rely on.
confirmed.verdict:
I could not refute it. The defect is real but low severity: it loses the record of the pilot's cut, not anything that reaches the game.

Code: bridges_v31.py:50 sets H0 to the heights of the input terrain. bridges_v31.py:116 then writes arrays['v31_bridge_cut'] = H != H0, which replaces the mask loaded from the input at :49 and never ORs the old one in. So the mask only marks what the current run changed.

Real inputs: E:/DayZ-Baltic-Build/v31-pond-layer-20261013/ev108-kit/terrain-ev108.npz already carries v31_bridge_cut with 23 vertices set. Those are the pilot's cut, also 23 in bridges/terrain-ev107.npz.

Reproduction: I ran the unmodified tool (gis-env python -I) on terrain-ev108.npz and envelope-ev108.npy with an empty sites list, writing to my scratchpad. The input mask had 23 vertices, the output mask had 0, and the heights were bit-identical (np.array_equal). A real rollout run has the same problem. Its new cuts only lower vertices at the 12 rollout sites, and a min() re-cut over the pilot vertices would leave them unchanged. Either way the pilot's 23 flags drop out.

Scope: heights, poses, pitch, the cut and seal cells, the envelope, records.json and staging are all unaffected. The mask is also correct for the 12 new sites. A grep of the worktree finds no other reader of v31_bridge_cut. The only loss is the separate layer that project rule 4 asks to keep before regenerating. That loss happens in the rollout run's output, and what it erases is the pilot's cut record. Fix: OR in the incoming mask when it exists, e.g. (H != H0) | arrays.get('v31_bridge_cut', False).

confirmed.title: The cut channel stops at |t| = 25 m and a straight band, so for 9 of the 12 rollout sites the sealed pool under the bridge is cut off from the stream on at least one side
confirmed.scenario: Rollout on EV108 V7 with the CSV rows. The cut only lowers vertices with |t| <= CUT_T (= 25, line 23) along a straight axis that has the fixed CSV water bearing. Only vertices within W/2 + (L-bed)/BANK = W/2 + 1 m of that axis go below the level (lines 91 and 94). The EV102 road cones left the stream dry well past 25 m, the real stream curves, and on the 6 m grid a 5.5-6.3 m wet band can only touch the stream at a NE-SW corner, which is not an edge of the native triangles. The sealed cells at L become a pond only under the deck, with an uncut ridge between that pond and the existing stream water. The report cannot catch this: channel_ground_max_under_deck (line 110) only looks at |s| <= flat and reads bed level (1.0-1.95) at dammed sites such as 015-4, 015-13, 015-16 and 015-18.
confirmed.verdict:
The defect is real: at 9 of the 12 sites the pool cut and sealed under the bridge stays cut off from the stream by a ridge 0.2 to 2.3 m above the stream level. It affects the 12-site rollout, not the pilot.

**Code reading** (tools/terrain/bridges_v31.py):
- Line 95 limits the lowering to `zone = |t| <= CUT_T`, with CUT_T = 25 (line 23).
- Line 94 sets the target to `bed + BANK*(|q| - W/2)`, so only a narrow straight band along the fixed CSV water bearing ends up below L.
- Line 105 limits the seals to the same |t| <= 25.
- Nothing joins the channel to the existing stream water beyond 25 m.
- The `under` metric on line 110 is bounded by |s| <= flat and |q| <= W/2. At sites 16 and 18 it reads the bed (1.2 and 1.0), so the report shows nothing wrong there.

**Reproduction.** I ran the unmodified tool in scratch on ev108-kit/terrain-ev108.npz and envelope-ev108.npy, using the 12 plan rows of crossings-ev106.csv. Metal x2 sites were entered once, and also as two spans at ±12.5 m; the result is the same. I then took the minimax pass (N4 plus the NW-SE diagonal) from the lowest vertex under the deck to any vertex that is wet under the original envelope, with |t| > 28 and a level within 0.3 m of L. Pass minus L, for the +t / -t side (site ids are the CSV n column):

| 015-8 | -0.19 | +1.14 |
| 015-11 | +0.02 | +0.08 |

| 015-25 | +0.33 | -0.16 |

This matches the reviewer's figures to within a few cm, except 015-4 -t (1.53 here, 1.77 for the reviewer).

**Profile along the axis.** The blocking vertices are ev102_raised road-cone embankment just past the cut:

confirmed.title: 'bridge_metal_25 x2' cannot be expressed: the channel axis, flat band and seals all come from the single site point
confirmed.scenario: Four rollout sites (4, 8, 11, 13) need two 25 m spans end to end. Each site entry yields one record. Its q/t frame (lines 78-81), the frozen exception |s| <= half-6.5 (lines 92-93 and 98) and the seal (line 105) are all centred on that entry's x,z. (a) Two entries offset +-12.5 m along the road, the only way to get two records: each entry cuts and seals its own channel parallel to the real stream, displaced 12.5*sin(angle) = 9.3-12.4 m from it. The real stream axis under the joint stays at road height. (b) One entry at the crossing: only one 25 m span is placed, and flat = 6 m. Frozen corridor vertices on the stream axis at |s| = 6.6-14.5 stay at road height inside the sealed channel, partly under the deck and partly beyond its ends. Even vertices at |s| 6.6-7.5 stay uncut, though they lie inside the metal deck's clear opening: LOD0 reaches down to y=-12.4 only at |z| >= ~8.3, and the roadway is flat at 8.05 over the full +-12.5.
confirmed.verdict:
The claim holds. It affects 4 of the 12 rollout sites (015-4, 8, 11 and 13, plan 'bridge_metal_25 x2') and does not affect the pilot, which is a single bridge_wood_25.

Code reading (tools/terrain/bridges_v31.py):
- Each site entry yields exactly one record (line 72). The entry schema has no span count or offset (docstring line 4).
- The bridge centre, the channel frame (lines 78-81: t/q are relative to the entry's x,z), the frozen-vertex exception (lines 92-93 and 98: |s| <= half - 6.5 = 6.0 m for metal) and the seal (lines 103-105) are all centred on that one point.
- Two spans end to end can therefore only be written in two ways, and both give the wrong output:
  (a) Two entries offset +-12.5 m along the road. Each entry cuts and seals a channel parallel to the stream but through its own point, so neither channel lies on the real stream.
  (b) One entry at the crossing. Only one 25 m span is placed, and the frozen corridor vertices at |s| > 6 stay uncut inside the sealed channel.

Reproduction: I ran the unmodified tool with gis-env python -I on the real EV108 inputs (terrain-ev108.npz, envelope-ev108.npy). Site points, bearings, width and level came from the 'x2' rows of crossings-ev106.csv. Outputs went to the scratchpad only (x2.py, sites-one/two.json, rep-*.json).
- Case (a): stream-axis vertices with |q| <= W/2 and |t| <= 25 that still sit above the pond level L:
  - 015-4: 12/12, max 7.4 m vs L 2.45
  - 015-8: 11/11, max 12.28 m vs L 5.425
  - 015-11: 8/8, max 11.35 m vs L 3.0
  - 015-13: 15/16, max 8.15 m vs L 1.775
- Case (b): stream-axis vertices still above L: 4/12 at 015-4, 1/11 at 015-8, 0/8 at 015-11, 5/16 at 015-13. The maximum is 7.4 / 11.83 / 8.19 m. The seal is written over these cells at level L.
- Both runs classify all four sites as pond, so the seal is written in each case.

Case (b) also does not place the planned two spans. Whichever way the 4 sites are expressed, the cut and seal cells are wrong for them.

Not checked here:
- The claimed ODOL metal LOD0 profile (the clear opening at |z| 6-8).
- Footprint and exposed-edge counts.

These details only add to the claim; they are not needed to confirm it.

confirmed.title: 'bridge_metal_25 x2' cannot be expressed: channel and seal are tied to the bridge centre, so two offset spans dam the real stream at their joint
confirmed.scenario: Four rollout crossings (CSV n4, n8, n11, n13) are planned as 'bridge_metal_25 x2', meaning two 25 m spans end to end. Narva already does this: the EV108 WRP holds 9 bridge_metal_25 records spaced 25 m apart. bridges_v31.py places exactly one model per site entry (lines 53-72). It also builds the water axis and cut window from the same s['x'], s['z'] (lines 78-81: t, q; line 92: sroad; line 93: flat = half - 6.5). So the only way to get two spans is two entries at C +/- 12.5 m along the road. Each entry then cuts and seals a channel through its own span centre, about 12 m from the stream. The real crossing sits at the joint, |sroad| = 12.5 > flat = 6.0 for both entries, so its frozen road vertices are never lowered. Result: two dry or isolated side channels and the stream still dammed under the bridge. The other option, one entry at the crossing, places a single 25 m span instead of the planned 50 m.
confirmed.verdict:
The defect is real. It affects 4 of the 12 rollout sites (CSV n4, n8, n11, n13, planned as 'bridge_metal_25 x2'). It does not affect the pilot, which is one bridge_wood_25 span at #15.

Code reading, tools/terrain/bridges_v31.py:
- Each site entry places exactly one model, centred on C = (s.x, s.z) (lines 53-72).
- The channel and seal geometry are built from that same centre: the window at line 78, X_/Z_ at line 80, the water-axis coordinates t and q at line 81, the seal at lines 103-105.
- Frozen road vertices may only be cut where |sroad| <= flat = half - 6.5 = 6.0 m around that same centre (lines 92-93, 98).
- The site schema has no span count or offset (docstring line 4).

So two end-to-end spans can only be written as two entries at C +/- 12.5 m along the road. Each entry then cuts its own channel, parallel to the stream but displaced from it. The real crossing at the joint (|sroad| = 12.5 > 6.0 for both entries) keeps its frozen road vertices. The other way to write it, one entry at C, places only one 25 m span instead of the planned 50 m.

Independent repro on the real V7 inputs: ev108-kit/terrain-ev108.npz and envelope-ev108.npy. Sites were built from crossings-ev106.csv with the CSV level, width and bearings. Scripts: scratchpad/refute-x2/mk.py, scratchpad/refute-x2/chk.py; run outputs in scratchpad/refute-x2/{double,single}. Python: gis-env -I.

Two entries offset +/-12.5 m. Ground before->after along the road at s = -12 / 0 / +6 / +12 m (F = frozen vertex):
- n4: 7.37->1.95 / 7.39->7.39 / 7.40->7.40 / 7.40->1.95
- n8: 12.95->4.93 / 12.20->12.20 / 11.91->11.91 / 11.67->4.93
- n11: 11.52->2.50 / 11.34->11.34 / 11.31->11.31 / 11.30->2.50
- n13: 8.26->1.27 / 8.11->8.11 / 8.11->8.11 / 8.14->1.27

So the road is cut into a ditch under each span centre, about 12 m from the stream. Meanwhile the true crossing at s = 0 (and s = +6) stays at road height, all on frozen road vertices. The stream is still dammed under the joint. Each entry also writes its own seal cells (26-36 per entry) over those side channels.

One entry at the crossing cuts in the right place (n4 s=0: 7.39->1.95; n8 12.20->4.93; n11 11.34->2.50; n13 8.11->1.27), but only one 25 m span is placed.

Any input to this script therefore gives a wrong result for the four x2 sites. The 8 single-span bridge_wood_25 sites are not affected by this issue.

confirmed.title: Report field channel_ground_max_under_deck reads stream-bed vertices up to ~50 m from the road, not under the deck
confirmed.scenario: The mask is under = (|sroad| <= flat) & (|q| <= W/2) (line 110). It has no bound on lateral distance from the road and no |t| <= CUT_T bound. For a near-perpendicular crossing, the whole stream axis in the +/-66 m window counts as 'under the deck', so the field reports uncut bed far upstream or downstream. The pilot's report.json and the rollout reports then misstate whether the channel under the deck is open, which is the evidence used to accept the sites.
confirmed.verdict:
The claim holds, but only for the report. Terrain, envelope and records are unaffected.

What the code does: in tools/terrain/bridges_v31.py:110, under = (|sroad| <= flat) & (|q| <= W/2). Nothing limits the distance from the road (the lateral offset) and nothing limits |t| to CUT_T. When the road is roughly perpendicular to the stream, sroad is about ±q, so every stream-axis vertex in the ±66 m window (k = 11 cells) counts as "under the deck". Inside |t| <= 25, line 100 always cuts those vertices to the bed, because allowed holds wherever |sroad| <= flat. So any value above the bed reported at line 114 must come from uncut ground with |t| > CUT_T, away from the deck.

Reproduction (my own chk.py in the scratchpad, gis-env python -I):
- Pilot, bridges/terrain-ev107.npz, site 015-15: the masked maximum is 2.88 at t = -29.6, lateral -29.5. This matches report.json. Inside the deck footprint (|lateral| <= 4.02) and inside |t| <= CUT_T the maximum is 0.0, which is the sea-mode bed.
- Rollout: I ran the unmodified bridges_v31.py on ev108-kit/terrain-ev108.npz and envelope-ev108.npy, with sites built from the bridge rows of crossings-ev106.csv, writing into the scratchpad. Six of 14 sites report a value that is not the bed:

| site | reported | bed | vertex location | deck footprint max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| n5 | 5.5 | 1.75 | t 62.5, lat -62.6 | 1.75 |
| n11 | 3.4 | 2.5 | t 52.8 | 2.5 |
| n15 (pilot site) | 2.88 | 0.0 | t -29.6 | 0.0 |
| n19 | 9.18 | 4.225 | t 37.4, lat -36.5 | 4.22 |
| n25 | 4.31 | 1.575 | t 26.6 | 1.58 |
| n37 | 6.58 | 4.15 | t 35.9 | 4.15 |

At every site, the deck footprint and the |t| <= CUT_T zone come out at exactly the bed. The other eight sites report the bed correctly.

Impact: this is a report-only error. The pose, pitch, cut, seals, frozen-vertex handling and sea/pond mode are all unchanged. However, channel_ground_max_under_deck in report.json is wrong for the pilot and for 5 rollout sites. It makes the channel under the deck look blocked when it is open at the bed. Anyone accepting sites from this field would wrongly reject or query n5, n11, n19, n25 and n37.

Not verified: how "metal x2" (two spans) is meant to be represented in sites.json. I ran those rows as a single bridge_metal_25 at the crossing point. No files in the repo were modified.

rejected.title: Channel cut lowers the ground under the metal deck's end edges, leaving the 12 m roadway hanging up to 1.9-3.2 m above the terrain
rejected.reason:
The measurement holds, but the defect does not. The cut does lower the ground under the metal deck's outer end corners. What the reviewer calls a hanging roadway is a corner over a bank, and the model's own legs already support that corner. Pose, pitch, height and the deck-to-road contact are all unchanged.

How I checked: I ran bridges_v31.main from a copy in my scratch directory. Inputs were the EV108 V7 terrain and envelope plus the 13 planned crossings-ev106 rows (12 rollout sites and pilot 015-15), in a single-span variant and a split variant (two spans with centres at ±12.5 m along the road). I put the roadway LOD (3e15) vertices through the output matrices and measured each vertex's height above tri_h(H0) and tri_h(H_out).

1. **The gap growth reproduces.** The `allowed` mask at bridges_v31.py:98 lowers non-frozen vertices that sit outside |sroad| <= flat. That includes the shoulders next to the metal deck ends. Worst outer-end vertices:
   - Single span, site 4: from about +0.3 to +2.2 m (up to 2.43 m).
   - Split spans: 4b about +3.0/3.5 m, 11a +1.98 m, 11b +1.95 m, 13a -0.01 to +1.28 m.
   - Site 8: unaffected.

   Wood decks and the pilot end within -0.0..+0.12 m. The centre of the roadway at both ends stays on the frozen road (the probe-verified axis contact), so the deck still meets the road.

2. **The geometry refutes the "hanging" claim.** The ODOL of bridge_metal_25 has corner legs in its geometry LOD (1e13) and visual LOD 1. They sit at x ±8.0..8.8 and z ±9.1..10.1 and ±11.5..12.5, which is right at the deck-end corners, and reach down to y = -12.4. The roadway is at y 8.05, so the legs go about 20.5 m below it. After the cut the ground under the corners is only about 2-3.5 m below the deck, so the legs still go deep into the terrain and the corners stay supported.

3. **What is left is cosmetic.** There is an open 2-3 m void beside the frozen road strip under the outer roadway and walkway edges, between the legs. That is a 1:2 bank, which is exactly the channel formula in the docstring (lines 9-11), next to a bridge standing on its own piers. It is not a wrong pose, pitch or height, not a deck failing to meet the road, not a frozen-vertex violation and not a seal or index error. The frozen road vertices under the ends are outside `flat` and are not cut.

**Rollout:** the extra void appears only at metal sites 4, 11 and 13 (more so with the split-span layout) and is visual only. It does not touch the pilot or the 8 wood rollout sites.

**Not checked:** the in-game look, and how the rollout will actually encode "x2"; I assumed centres at ±12.5 m.

Side note: my first runs wrote these files into the shared scratch root, possibly overwriting files of the same name from another session: sites-single.json, sites-split.json, t-single.npz, t-split.npz, e-single.npy, e-split.npy, rec-single.json, rec-split.json, rep-single.json, rep-split.json. My scripts are in scratchpad/refute_edge/. No repo file was edited.

rejected.title: stage_bridges_v31.py stages the new heights on the base water ('same water'), which only holds for sea-mode sites; with pond seals the channels come out dry and existing piece edges are exposed
rejected.reason:
This is a documented precondition, not a code defect. stage_bridges_v31.py:1 says it stages "on top of an already staged v31 WRP (same water)". Lines 18-19 copy the base tree, swap in the heights and append the bridge records. It is meant to run after the water stage, not instead of it. The water stage is tools/water/stage_pond_pilot_v31.py. That script takes the terrain and the authored pieces and restages heights plus water records ("--full" replaces every baltic_water_v30 record).

The real builds show this order. ev108/stage-report.json was produced by stage_bridges_v31.py. It re-adds the bridge 015-15 plus the kit records on top of base_wrp_sha256 926044…, which is the water tree restaged after the kit pilot changed the envelope. ev108-kit/stage-water.log shows that water stage: 15089 dropped, 13508 added. The rollout follows the same chain. E:/DayZ-Baltic-Build/v31-pond-layer-20261013/ev109 already has bridge-records.json, envelope-br.npy, terrain-br.npz, terrain-ev109.npz and bury-report.json, and fp-ev109 has been created but is still empty. So the next steps are footprint, then authoring, then the water stage on terrain-ev109, then stage_bridges. Nothing in the rollout stages the new heights under the EV108 pond pieces.

The reviewer's numbers do not apply. They come from the old EV108 footprint planes (fp0) on the new terrain, a combination this pipeline never ships: the footprint is recomputed from the new terrain plus the envelope that now carries the seals. The bury step on the real rollout inputs (ev109/bury-report.json) reports exposed=43, new=[] and changed_vs_input=0. That matches the EV106 baseline of 43 and contradicts the claimed jump from 43 to 71.

The pilot (EV107) was in sea mode with no seals, so keeping the same water was correct there; the reviewer agrees. The only risk left is an operator running stage_bridges on a base tree that was never restaged. That would be a misuse of a documented contract, not output the code gets wrong. The script has no check that the base water matches the envelope; adding one would be hardening, not a bug fix.

rejected.title: v31_bridge_cut is overwritten with only the current run's changes, so the EV107 pilot's cut layer is lost when rolling out on EV108
rejected.reason:
The mechanics the reviewer describes are accurate, but this is not a defect within the scope of the review. It changes no output that the rollout or the pilot uses.

1. What I checked by reading the code. In tools/terrain/bridges_v31.py:50, H0 is this run's input heights. Line 116 sets `arrays["v31_bridge_cut"] = H != H0`, which replaces any mask that came in with the input instead of merging into it.

2. What I checked on the real files. I loaded both npz files with the gis-env python. bridges/terrain-ev107.npz (the pilot output) and ev108-kit/terrain-ev108.npz (the rollout input) both already contain v31_bridge_cut, with 23 True vertices each. So after the 12-site run the output mask will show only that run's cuts. I did not rerun the reviewer's 12-site test, so their figures of 261 vertices and 0 of 23 kept are not reproduced here. The code at line 116 guarantees the pilot's mask is not carried over either way.

3. Why it is not a defect.
- The pilot's channel is not lost. It already lives in the heights the run starts from (H0), and the run only lowers heights (`np.minimum`, line 100). So the pilot cut survives in the output heights.
- None of the outputs that matter change: heights, envelope seals, sea/pond classification, records.json (pose and matrix) and the staged WRP.
- Grep across the worktree finds only one reference to v31_bridge_cut: the writer at line 116. Nothing reads it, so no regeneration step depends on it.
- It is a per-run diagnostic mask, the same way every other stage in this pipeline writes one: `ev101_sea_bed_smoothed = ch` (smooth_sea_bed_ev101.py:76), `ev102_raised = ch` (sills_and_cones_ev102.py:218), `v31_lake_rim_lowered = ch` (lower_lake_rims_v31.py:76). It is not a stored retouch layer under rule 4.

At most this is a record-keeping detail. If the mask should ever keep a history across runs, line 116 could OR it with the incoming mask (`arrays.get("v31_bridge_cut", False) | (H != H0)`). Neither the 12-site rollout nor the pilot is affected.

rejected.title: stage_bridges_v31 assumes the base WRP already has 'the same water'; every rollout site seals new pond cells and nothing checks it
rejected.reason:
Refuted. This is a precondition the tool states, not a code defect. stage_bridges_v31.py:1 says it stages bridges "on top of an already staged v31 WRP (same water)". Lines 11-19 only swap heights and append records, which is exactly that job. Pond seals become water through a separate step: bridges_v31.py writes them into out_envelope (bridges_v31.py:106-107, 116), and the pond pipeline (footprint/bury, author, stage_pond_pilot_v31.py --full) turns that envelope into pond pieces. The README says the same: "Puentes de 015: las aperturas bajo el tablero irán como sellos de esta envolvente."

The EV108 build already follows this order and avoids both failures the reviewer describes. First, ev108-kit/stage-water.log ran stage_pond --full on base a7d8a91b with terrain b2d9f8e7, which gave WRP 92604450. Then ev108/stage-report.json used 92604450 as the base for stage_bridges with the same terrain b2d9f8e7, so the water already matched the envelope when the bridge and kit records were appended.

Duplication does not happen either. I counted the records in both staged WRPs with wrp0wzd.read: EV107 and EV108 each hold exactly 1 bridge_wood_25 and 9 bridge_metal_25 (the Narva spans), and all ids are unique (13789 of 13789 in EV107, 13701 of 13701 in EV108). So the pilot bridge was not appended twice.

The rollout work in E:/DayZ-Baltic-Build/v31-pond-layer-20261013/ev109 also re-runs the pond steps on the bridge output: envelope-br.npy, terrain-br.npz, bury.log, bury-report.json and bury-work/fp0. Its bridges.log has extra fields (spans, cut_t, links), so it was produced by a newer bridges script than the one in this worktree.

The reviewer's repro is right that some cells have NaN in the EV108 footprint. I did not re-run it, so the count of 183 is unconfirmed. Either way, that only shows the EV108 water does not cover the new seals. That is expected and is the reason the pond restage step exists. The tool would ship dry trenches only if someone skipped that step, which goes against the tool's stated contract and the established EV108 recipe. That is a misuse scenario, not a defect in the code's output. It does not affect the pilot, which is in sea mode with no seal, and it does not affect the rollout when the documented pipeline is used.
